I have been growing cotton on this land my whole farming life. Thirty-five years — I know the soil here, I know how to read the weather, I know when the cotton needs water and when it doesn't. My father grew cotton, and his father before him. Quzhou soil is good for it.

I will put most of my land — 13 mu — into cotton, same as always. The rest, about 3 mu, I'll keep in stevia. The stevia contract gives steady money and my daughter-in-law handles most of that work. She knows it better than me now.

For cotton, I'll use the hybrid Bt seed I've been buying from the county supply station for the past several years. It's more expensive than the old seed but I lose less to bollworm. Four fertilizer applications through the season — base before planting, then top-dress twice, light potassium late. I don't over-water. Four irrigations from my well is enough if timing is right: seedling, budding, flowering, boll-filling. I skip the fifth if there's any late-season rain. Pesticide four times — aphids come no matter what, and I watch for red spider mites in July.

For stevia I do less. The plants come back strong from the roots. Two cuttings of leaf per season. I irrigate more often but lighter each time — five times. Fewer pests on stevia so two spray rounds is enough.

I do rotary tillage on both plots in spring before planting. My son helps me with that.
